data.hypothesis: The prior valid static-worksharing candidate with a 256-element-per-worker dispatch threshold measured 0.071596 seconds; direct contiguous ranges at that threshold measured 0.072476 seconds. Those whole-call measurements are close and do not establish the scheduler as the cause. This contrasting candidate keeps static scheduling but lowers the per-worker threshold to 64, testing whether parallelizing n=128 with two workers (while keeping n=16 serial) amortizes dispatch overhead; worker count remains bounded by the supplied threads budget. The new candidate is unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: Independent per-element pricing can use static outer-loop worksharing while limiting parallel dispatch by both input size and the supplied thread budget.
memory_lessons.claim: Two valid candidates measured 0.071596 seconds with static worksharing and a 256-element threshold, and 0.072476 seconds with direct contiguous partitioning at the same threshold. Both were correct; this small observed difference is not proof of a scheduling cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 64-element threshold candidate against the 256-element static candidate using whole-call timings for the same n/thread cases, especially n=128 and the largest workload.

data.notes: Only the supplied measured outcomes are available: baseline 0.390983 seconds, static worksharing with threshold 256 at 0.071596 seconds, and direct contiguous partitioning with threshold 256 at 0.072476 seconds; all three were reported valid and correct. No failed scheduling or threshold variants appear in the supplied records, and no timing is available for this threshold-64 candidate. Request controller comparison of complete calls over the workload and n/threads cases; do not infer a speedup before those measurements.
transformations: Factored the unchanged per-input binomial pricing calculation into a helper with private stack-local intermediates, allowing independent calls from serial and parallel paths.
Retained a serial path for counts below 128 or a caller thread budget of one.
For larger calls, requested min(threads, count / 64) workers and used static OpenMP loop scheduling; each iteration fully overwrites its corresponding result, without changing global OpenMP controls.
